description: What the infrastructure benchmarks measure, by results file: the setup of each benchmark and what every row and variant of its table is. scripts/summarize.py renders it as the legend of the Benchmarks page; a benchmark, workload or variant added to the code is described here.

search.setup: A stock runner, First Improvement or Best Improvement, on two problems of the EasyLocal examples. The variants are the ways the runner reaches the moves of the neighborhood.

Domains.assignment: Assignment, 96 jobs on 8 machines, job reassignment moves

Algorithms.first-improvement: `runners::FirstImprovement`, which applies the first improving move of each scan
Algorithms.best-improvement: `runners::BestImprovement`, which scans the whole neighborhood and applies its best move

Variants.raw-cursor: the algorithm written by hand, calling the explorer's `first_move` and `next_move` directly, without a range and outside the runner framework: the reference the others are measured against
Variants.cursor-range: the stock runner iterating `easylocal::moves`, which turns the example's `first_move`/`next_move` cursor into a lazy range holding one move, without materializing the neighborhood: the difference from `raw-cursor` is the cost of the range and the runner
Variants.coroutine-range: the stock runner on an explorer whose `moves()` is a coroutine (`easylocal::generator`), as a user would write it

traversal.setup: The moves of a whole neighborhood, visited without a runner.

Domains.assignment-medium: Assignment, 256 jobs on 32 machines, job reassignment moves

Workloads.traversal: reads only the fields of each move, so the time is the cost of producing the moves
Workloads.light-consumer: also reads the data of the solution and of the instance the move touches (demands and capacities, distances), as a minimal evaluation would

Variants.coroutine-std: `moves()` as a `std::generator`, where the standard library provides it

trace.setup: A First Improvement run on an Assignment instance of 96 jobs on 8 machines, traced by each tracer; "without" is the same run with no tracer argument.

Tracers.explicit-null: `trace::null_tracer` passed explicitly; it should cost nothing
Tracers.counting: a tracer that only counts the events: the cost of producing them
Tracers.binary-buffered-discard: `trace::buffered_binary_recorder` (the ELTR binary format) writing to a stream that discards the bytes: encoding and buffering without input/output
Tracers.binary-buffered-discard-visited: the same, on a problem with a solution hash, which records a `solution_visited` event with the hash of each solution the search moves to
Tracers.binary-buffered-discard-without-visits: the same problem, with `solution_visited` left out at compile time (`trace::without<event::solution_visited>`); it should cost what `binary-buffered-discard` costs
Tracers.binary-async-producer-discard: `trace::async_binary_recorder`, which hands the events to a writer thread, writing to a discarding stream; the time of the search until it ends
Tracers.binary-async-total-discard: the same, also waiting for the writer to finish
Tracers.binary-async-producer-file: `trace::async_binary_recorder` writing a temporary file; the time of the search until it ends
Tracers.binary-async-total-file: the same, also waiting for the writer to finish

trace-cost-encoding.setup: A `move_evaluated` event, which carries the current and the candidate cost, encoded one million times in the ELTR binary format; bytes/event is the size of the encoded event.

Costs.hierarchical-2xi64-plus-i64: a `cost::hierarchical` with that lexicographic cost as hard cost and a 64-bit integer as soft cost
